name: MeasureTheory
integral_mul_norm_le_Lp_mul_Lq
result.signature:
{E} [NormedAddCommGroup E] {f g : α → E} {p q : ℝ} (hpq : p.HolderConjugate q) (hf : MemLp f (ENNReal.ofReal p) μ)
  (hg : MemLp g (ENNReal.ofReal q) μ) :
  ∫ a, ‖f a‖ * ‖g a‖ ∂μ ≤ (∫ a, ‖f a‖ ^ p ∂μ) ^ (1 / p) * (∫ a, ‖g a‖ ^ q ∂μ) ^ (1 / q)
result.type:
∀ {α : Type u_1} {m : MeasurableSpace α} {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure α} {E : Type u_6} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E]
  {f g : α → E} {p q : ℝ},
  p.HolderConjugate q →
    MeasureTheory.MemLp f (ENNReal.ofReal p) μ →
      MeasureTheory.MemLp g (ENNReal.ofReal q) μ →
        ∫ (a : α), ‖f a‖ * ‖g a‖ ∂μ ≤ (∫ (a : α), ‖f a‖ ^ p ∂μ) ^ (1 / p) * (∫ (a : α), ‖g a‖ ^ q ∂μ) ^ (1 / q)
result.value:
:= by
  -- translate the Bochner integrals into Lebesgue integrals.
  
  rw [integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae, integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae]
  rotate_left
  · exact Eventually.of_forall fun x => Real.rpow_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) _
  · exact (hg.1.norm.aemeasurable.pow aemeasurable_const).aestronglyMeasurable
  · exact Eventually.of_forall fun x => Real.rpow_nonneg (norm_nonneg _) _
  · exact (hf.1.norm.aemeasurable.pow aemeasurable_const).aestronglyM...
result.informal_description: For Hölder conjugate exponents $ p $ and $ q $ (i.e., $ \frac{1}{p} + \frac{1}{q} = 1 $), if $ f \in L^p(\mu, E) $ and $ g \in L^q(\mu, E) $, then the integral of the product of their norms satisfies $ \int \|f(a)\| \cdot \|g(a)\| \, d\mu(a) \leq \left(\int \|f(a)\|^p \, d\mu(a)\right)^{1/p} \cdot \left(\int \|g(a)\|^q \, d\mu(a)\right)^{1/q} $.

name: real_inner_le_norm
result.type: ∀ {F : Type u_3} [inst : SeminormedAddCommGroup F] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ F] (x y : F), inner ℝ x y ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖
result.informal_name: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality for Real Inner Products
result.informal_description: For any vectors $x$ and $y$ in a real inner product space $F$, the inner product $\langle x, y \rangle$ satisfies $\langle x, y \rangle \leq \|x\| \cdot \|y\|$.

name: nnnorm_inner_le_nnnorm
result.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] [inst_1 : SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_2 : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
  (x y : E), ‖inner 𝕜 x y‖₊ ≤ ‖x‖₊ * ‖y‖₊
result.informal_name: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality for Inner Product Spaces
result.informal_description: For all vectors $x$ and $y$ in an inner product space $E$, the non-negative norm of their inner product satisfies $\|\langle x, y \rangle\|_+ \leq \|x\|_+ \cdot \|y\|_+$, where $\|\cdot\|_+$ denotes the non-negative norm.

name: norm_inner_le_norm
result.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} {E : Type u_2} [inst : RCLike 𝕜] [inst_1 : SeminormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_2 : InnerProductSpace 𝕜 E]
  (x y : E), ‖inner 𝕜 x y‖ ≤ ‖x‖ * ‖y‖
result.value:
:= by
  rw [norm_eq_sqrt_re_inner (𝕜 := 𝕜) x, norm_eq_sqrt_re_inner (𝕜 := 𝕜) y]
  letI : PreInnerProductSpace.Core 𝕜 E := PreInnerProductSpace.toCore
  exact InnerProductSpace.Core.norm_inner_le_norm x y
result.informal_name: Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality for Inner Product Spaces
result.informal_description: For any vectors $x$ and $y$ in an inner product space $E$ over a real closed field-like scalar field $\mathbb{K}$, the absolute value of their inner product is less than or equal to the product of their norms, i.e., $|\langle x, y \rangle| \leq \|x\| \cdot \|y\|$.

name: intervalIntegral
norm_integral_le_of_norm_le
result.signature:
{g : ℝ → ℝ} (hab : a ≤ b) (h : ∀ᵐ t ∂μ, t ∈ Set.Ioc a b → ‖f t‖ ≤ g t) (hbound : IntervalIntegrable g μ a b) :
  ‖∫ t in a..b, f t ∂μ‖ ≤ ∫ t in a..b, g t ∂μ
result.type:
∀ {E : Type u_5} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : NormedSpace ℝ E] {a b : ℝ} {f : ℝ → E}
  {μ : MeasureTheory.Measure ℝ} {g : ℝ → ℝ},
  a ≤ b →
    (∀ᵐ (t : ℝ) ∂μ, t ∈ Set.Ioc a b → ‖f t‖ ≤ g t) →
      IntervalIntegrable g μ a b → ‖∫ (t : ℝ) in a..b, f t ∂μ‖ ≤ ∫ (t : ℝ) in a..b, g t ∂μ
result.value:
:= by
  simp only [integral_of_le hab, ← ae_restrict_iff' measurableSet_Ioc] at *
  exact MeasureTheory.norm_integral_le_of_norm_le hbound.1 h
result.informal_name: Bound on the norm of an interval integral via a majorant
result.informal_description:
Let `E` be a real Banach space, `f : ℝ → E` and `g : ℝ → ℝ` be two functions, and `μ` be a measure on `ℝ`. For any `a, b ∈ ℝ` with `a ≤ b`, if `g` is integrable on the interval from `a` to `b` and `‖f(t)‖ ≤ g(t)` for almost every `t` in the interval `(a, b]` with respect to `μ`, then the norm of the interval integral of `f` from `a` to `b` is bounded by the interval integral of `g` from `a` to `b`:
$$
\left\|\int_a^b f(t) \, d\mu\right\| \le \int_a^b g(t) \, d\mu
$$
